newsitem.title: USA: U.S. explains delay in Zaire decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. explains delay in Zaire decision.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday the complexity of the Zaire humanitarian crisis and the need for a solution that "makes sense" was holding up a decision on supporting a multinational intervention force aimed at saving more than one million refugees.

State Department Deputy Spokesman Glyn Davies said at a news briefing that repatriating the refugees to Rwanda must be part of an international solution to the crisis, which U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and others insist demands immediate action.

U.S. officials said an assessment team headed by U.S. Army Major General Edward Smith, commander of the South European Task Force based in Vicenza, Italy, would arrive in Central Africa on Wednesday to examine the situation.

Davies said the mix of militias, ethnic groups and refugees along Zaire's border with Rwanda had produced a "very complex situation. And the essence of it for the United States is deciding what makes sense to do, what can we do, and then to make a decision whether or not to go ahead and do that. I mean that decision has yet to be made."

"The challenge is putting the various components together so that you actually have something that can go into that very remote mountainous part of the world and work. And that's ... the challenge, that's the puzzle, if you will, putting together something that will work, that will take best advantage of what the various players can bring to the mission," he said.
Davies added: "And it's not simply a question of parachuting in foodstuffs or water to people because in this situation, unlike other situations, we're not even sure where the people are."
